title: Sensor Calibration Exception Rate
dataSources: Pump telemetry (`health:glucose`), lab results (`health:lab`), therapy sessions (`health:pt`), symptom diaries (`health:symptom`), care tasks (`health:ops`).
app: Chronic-condition self-management telemetry — insulin-pump events, A1c lab imports, physical-therapy rep logs, and symptom diaries — streamed to Splunk HEC via device exports and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=health:glucose sensor_type=* calibration_exception=*
| stats count as total, sum(eval(if(calibration_exception="yes",1,0))) as matched by sensor_type
| eval a_calibration_exception_pct=round(100*matched/total,1)
| sort - a_calibration_exception_pct
description: Measures the percentage of sensor readings that end with a calibration exception by sensor type.
value: Completion and exception percentages make it easier to spot which sensor type are helping or hurting sensor readings.
implementation: Store a normalized flag for `a calibration exception` on `health:glucose` events and summarize the hit rate by `sensor_type`.
visualization: Table of sensor type with percentage of sensor readings ending with a calibration exception.
grandmaExplanation: It blends how often a calibration exception happens for each sensor type so you can see where sensor readings go smoothly or get stuck.
